Choose on evidence, not just taste

Three hypotheses.
One useful test.

ConceptWhat we’re testingWatch for
01 / GuideApproachability + immediate calculator value encourage exploration.Does the calculator attract relevant buyers, or only curiosity?
02 / MotionA visual demonstration makes the combination memorable.Can visitors explain the offer without watching a full loop?
03 / OutcomesRecognizing a business problem creates a stronger reason to talk.Do more of the conversations fit the work you want?

First: a comprehension test.

  1. Show one concept to each prospect for five seconds. Rotate the order across prospects.
  2. Ask: What do we do? Who is it for? Why choose us? What would you do next?
  3. Then let them explore. Observe where they click and where they hesitate.
  4. Use 5–8 relevant people per direction for qualitative feedback. This is not a statistically powered conversion experiment.

Then: measure real intent.

After the winning candidates have real booking and consent-aware analytics, split comparable traffic randomly. Hold the offer, audience and qualification criteria constant.

Primary measure: qualified conversations booked per unique visitor. Secondary: path selections, calculator completion and CTA-to-booking completion. Track attendance and eventual proposals separately. Choose sample size from the baseline rate and minimum effect worth detecting; don’t declare a winner from a handful of clicks.

A model that can grow with the client.

Conversation → focused diagnostic → scoped first build → measured improvement → ongoing work where useful. Brand work can open a store project; ecommerce can reveal workflow needs; AI can create room for consistent content. Scope and capacity should determine expansion, rather than selling every pillar up front. No pricing has been invented for these previews.

What is working in these previews

All three directions have responsive pages, working navigation, a transparent calculator and a local conversation-brief flow. The motion concept includes a pause control and reduced-motion support. Demo clicks are recorded only in this browser, without form text. These are design-test prototypes: no messages are sent, appointments booked, or real visitor analytics collected.

Before a public launch

Confirm the buyer priority and exact service scope. Add approved work samples, attributed outcomes and permitted logos. Verify the $3B claim’s wording and provenance before using it; it is deliberately absent here. Connect the agreed calendar and lead destination, add privacy/consent handling, verify a real lead receipt, and test the deployed experience on mobile and desktop. The earlier AskTony build was not recovered; concept 01 is an interpretation of its current product-first structure, not a replica.

Research behind the choices

Clarity earns the first click.

NN/g’s homepage guidance supports making the purpose legible at a glance. Progressive disclosure supports showing the important choices first, with detail available when needed. Applying these principles to concept 03 is a design hypothesis, not proof it will convert best.
